verdict.rationale: Babylon.js lists sprites and layers in its scene graph, which gives some 2D building blocks. Everything else in the pack frames it as a 3D engine: its physics integrations (Havok, Cannon.js, Ammo.js, Oimo.js) are 3D engines, and one user notes that 3D concepts are ingrained into the API. That makes 2D look like a secondary capability rather than a first-class workflow. Missing for 10: tilemap support, 2D physics, a dedicated 2D workflow or tooling, and in-depth sprite documentation or hands-on corroboration.
